title: Credit bundles and security-gated upgrade path experiment
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run an A/B/n experiment combining alternate free-credit bundles and a security-questionnaire (SQ) gated upgrade flow for enterprise signups. Objective: increase paid conversion from free tier signups with high intent while preserving product experience for self-serve users and capturing enterprise security signals earlier in the funnel. This ticket coordinates PM, Console UX, Growth analytics, and Eng work to implement credit allocation, expiry windows, contextual upgrade prompts, and SQ gating for teams that request dedicated capacity or contracts.
experiment_design: Three experimental arms: A (Baseline) = current 500 free credits, 30d expiry; B = larger bundle 2k credits, 30d expiry + subtle 'Recommended for teams' upgrade CTA; C = 2k credits, 60d expiry + contextual modal at 3 product events prompting 'Prepare for enterprise' which opens a lightweight SQ form. Randomize new signups 50/25/25 so baseline remains strong for power analysis. Primary metric: 30d paid conversion rate (upgrade to paid or contact sales). Secondary metrics: time-to-first-advanced-route call, enterprise lead capture rate, SQ completion %, NPS survey on onboarding. Success threshold: +18% relative lift in paid conversion for any test arm vs baseline with p<0.05 and no >5% regression in DAU retention.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: cohort tagging for experiment arm in signup flow and console UI events (created_at, credit_balance, expiry, CTA_shown).
Data: Analytics dashboard showing daily cohort conversion, SQ submissions, and revenue lift. Power calc validated for min detectable effect.
UX: modal and CTAs reviewed by Design (Lena Cho) and accessible (a11y) tested.
Security: lightweight SQ stores only non-PHI and flows into CRM with opt-in consent; Security review completed.
Rollout: experiment runs for minimum 21 days and meets power; winner approved by Growth + Sales for scaling to 100% rollout.

rollout_plan: Start as 50/25/25 randomized experiment for new signups. Monitor first 7 days for instrumentation correctness. If no data issues, run full 21-day window. Post-hoc analysis: holdback vs best-performing arm for an additional 14 days to validate revenue permanence. If SQ-gated arm increases enterprise leads >25% and Sales accepts lead quality, coordinate with Legal/Contracts to add 'express engagement' flow into AE playbook.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs: larger credit bundles risk increased short-term token expense with delayed revenue; longer expiries can reduce urgency and inflate free usage. SQ gating improves signal for Sales but may add friction and hurt conversion for SMB users — therefore SQ is only surfaced after repeated product events (intent-based trigger) and accepted by Sales for lead prioritization. Engineering complexity: SQ requires secure storage and new CRM integration (depends on ENG-1920).
